machine: Windows 11, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 Laptop GPU; engines in CHEMDRAW_ENGINE_HOME (CUDA builds of PyTorch where the engine has one); run on 2026-11-04
how: Every case was run through the toolkit tools (cdx.py call TOOL --json ...). wall_s is the whole command including starting the worker (about 5 to 10 s); engine_s is the time the engine itself reports, which includes loading the model, because an engine process is started for every call.
scope: Results are predictions. Each case is one run on the inputs named here, scored against a reviewed or recorded answer, with misses kept. They show how the engines behave, not how accurate they are.

ocsr.images: 13a.png, 16.png and 17.png are crops of the paper-replica original (third-party artwork, not relicensed); imatinib.png is a ChemDraw render of imatinib (imatinib.cdxml).
ocsr.reference: The structures drawn in assets/readme/paper-replica/replica.cdxml, whose five structures were checked against the original; R (on 13a) and X (on 16 and 17) are scored as the wildcard *, while SiMe2Ph on 13a is scored as the full silyl group.

decimer-local: installed in its own Python 3.11 + TensorFlow 2.15.1 (Keras 2.15) CPU environment under CHEMDRAW_ENGINE_HOME with both Zenodo weight archives verified by SHA-256; scored on all four OCSR images (matches imatinib and 17, misses 16 and 13a).

pdf.input: pages.pdf: assets/readme/paper-replica/original.png on page 1 and assets/readme/synthesis-113-122/reference.png on page 2 (third-party artwork), each placed on a landscape A4 page
pdf.segmenter: decimer-segmentation, structures read by molscribe and molvec

retro_forward_conditions.records: toolkit/samples/KL-CC-001 and KL-CC-002 (a Buchwald amination and an alkylation recorded in a lab notebook, with amounts and yields); imatinib is the published amide disconnection

caffeine.processing: Bruker processed spectra (pdata/1/1r) read with the scale in procs, trimmed to the shown window, thinned by taking every 6th to 16th point and written as ppm,intensity CSV scaled to 10000; the water signal of the caffeine 1H spectrum (4.3 to 5.3 ppm) is cut out. The CSV files here are those reduced copies.

nmrshiftdb2_20.entry: nmrshiftdb2 NMReDATA assigned export (20 molecules with paired 1H and 13C raw Bruker archives)
nmrshiftdb2_20.sample: 13 molecules in CDCl3, 7 molecules in DMSO-d6 (300 to 700 MHz 1H, 75 to 176 MHz 13C)
nmrshiftdb2_20.scoring: Assigned topological-group MAE over 215 non-exchangeable 1H (C-H) groups and 323 13C groups (exchangeable OH, NH and SH protons excluded on both sides; degenerate fast-exchange keto-enol tautomer symmetry applied on curcumin). Unassigned 1-to-1 Hungarian group matching is also recorded in benchmark20.json.
nmrshiftdb2_20.training_overlap: All 20 entries originate from nmrshiftdb2, which is part of NMRNet++'s supervised 5-fold CV training corpus (~80% per fold), and 7 of the 20 also pass NMRNet++'s ShiftDB-Lit (<=1 chiral center) filter; MagNET was trained strictly on synthetic AIMNet2/GIAO DFT shieldings with zero experimental NMR spectra.

lcms.source: PyParse v1.1.0 example dataset, Waters/Example1 (Zenodo, Apache-2.0; Mason et al., Digital Discovery 2023, doi 10.1039/D3DD00167A)
lcms.scope: The 2.3 MB report is not copied here; download the dataset and run match_plate.py.
